name: 100 gecs
label: Dog Show / Atlantic
lede: Two St. Louis friends swapped Logic files between Chicago and Los Angeles, and the closet-recorded album they made turned a pine tree in a Des Plaines office park into a pilgrimage site.

eras.title: Two laptops, two cities
eras.text: Dylan Brady and Laura Les met as friends of friends in the St. Louis suburbs, then spent years making music apart. Brady put out beat-scene SoundCloud tracks and label EPs; Les released records as osno1. The duo itself started as file swaps between Los Angeles and Chicago.

years.big: "I was so intimidated by how good he was."
q: I was so intimidated by how good he was.
years.src: The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy · Kerrang
years.h: Les goes home from a St. Louis house party feeling outclassed
years.p: Laura Les and Dylan Brady met in 2012 as friends of friends. Both grew up in the suburbs, Brady in Kirkwood and Les in Webster Groves, and her first move was to go home and work on music.
years.xp:
The FADER has Les describing the night: friends of friends at a St. Louis-area house party, and she left feeling outclassed.

Kerrang adds that they'd been circling the same Missouri scene for years, down to both being at a Van Halen reunion show without knowing each other.

years.h: Brady's first solo record is called All I Ever Wanted
years.p: He had been posting electronic hip-hop productions to SoundCloud while studying audio engineering. He also played in a band called Cake Pop, whose EP came out the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · Wikipedia: Laura Les · Wikipedia: Dylan Brady
years.h: The first gecs songs start as Logic files in Les's Chicago apartment
years.p: They traded sessions, each finishing what the other started. Les later called the method an exquisite corpse.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the start of 100 gecs to winter 2015, in Les's Chicago apartment, with Logic files passed back and forth. Les has described it as very much an improv mentality: write songs they'd want to listen to.

The Wikipedia pages for the two members give 2016 as the founding year, so the start date is soft.

years.h: A self-released 100 gecs EP comes first
years.p: The duo's first release. Les was meanwhile putting out records as osno1, including one about dead bodies.
years.xp:
Les released the osno1 EP hello kitty skates to the fuckin CEMETARY in 2016, which she described as a bunch of songs about dead bodies.

A follow-up, i just dont wanna name it anything with "beach" in the title, came in 2017, and she dropped the osno1 name in 2018.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dylan Brady · Wikipedia: Laura Les
years.h: Brady lands a Mad Decent EP while Vice notices Les
years.p: Brady's Peace & Love came out on Mad Decent. Les's BIG SUMMER JAMS 2018 EP drew a Vice write-up calling it debauched digital celebrations.

eras.title: A closet recording takes over 2019
eras.text: Brady in Los Angeles and Les in a Chicago closet made 1000 gecs mostly by email. It landed in the spring, and by December the argument over it was the year's biggest.

years.h: "Money Machine" shows up two days ahead of the album
years.p: Recorded in January 2019. Brady built the beat in Logic; Les says it struck her as sarcastic, with a bassline that seemed to be laughing at her.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account of the song: Les built her vocal from real-life frustration at work, borrowing the tone of a King of the Hill character, and Brady took the title from money he'd seen on the ground.

Pitchfork ranked it No. 61 on its 2019 songs list, and it later reached No. 47 on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs.

q: I still work at my full time job in a restaurant.
years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs · The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy
years.h: 1000 gecs: about 80 percent of it made remotely
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 7.4 and called it one of the year's most fascinating, exhilarating experimental pop albums.
years.xp:
Les recorded her vocals in her closet, pitch-shifted, which Wikipedia says she has tied to voice dysphoria. Brady and Les name John Zorn, Cannibal Corpse, YouTube and nightcore as reference points, and Brady called the record a best-of compilation.

The FADER caught Les just after release still working a full-time restaurant job.

years.h: A Des Plaines parking lot becomes the "Money Machine" video
years.p: Paper put it somewhere between a cybernetic hallucination and a deep fried meme. It was shot in the same office park as the album cover.

years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs · Wikipedia: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues
years.h: Free stems and a cappellas turn fans into remixers
years.p: The duo posted instrumentals and vocal stems of 1000 gecs, and the fan remixes started immediately.
years.xp: That release fed the remix album. Wikipedia says the follow-up was retitled in early 2020 after the duo found fan-made remixes of their stems.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · The FADER: The brilliant pop anarchy
years.h: The cover's pine tree is real, and fans bring offerings
years.p: It stands in an office park in Des Plaines, Illinois. People found it on Google Maps and started leaving things there.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the tree stands at an Acuity Brands-owned office park near O'Hare, and that fans made pilgrimages and left items behind. The Chicago Tribune compared the phenomenon to the house on American Football's 1999 cover.

The FADER noted fans found the coordinates, made memes, and started petitions.

years.cap: 100 gecs at the Armory, Minneapolis, December 3, 2019
years.h: They open for Brockhampton on the Heaven Belongs to You tour
years.p: Wikipedia lists them as support on the 2019 run, alongside slowthai, plus six headline dates along the route.

years.h: A.G. Cook remixes "Money Machine" and the wave starts
years.p: The PC Music founder's take was an early entry in the remix flood that became the Tree of Clues album.

years.h: They play for a green-screen aquarium on Adult Swim
years.p: On FishCenter Live they did "800db Cloud" and "Stupid Horse".

years.cap: 100 gecs at the Armory, Minneapolis, December 3, 2019
years.h: Jon Caramanica ranks it No. 1 of 2019 in the New York Times
years.p: Jon Pareles put 1000 gecs at No. 10 on his own list. Pitchfork and Stereogum also listed it.
years.xp: Rolling Stone had already named them an Artist You Need to Know that year. Wikipedia credits the record with popularizing hyperpop as a mainstream idea.

eras.title: Everyone remixes them, and Atlantic signs them
eras.text: With a whole scene working on their stems, the duo signed to Atlantic and put out a remix album with Charli XCX and Fall Out Boy. Les put out a solo single that ended up on Euphoria.

years.h: Charli XCX and Rico Nasty jump on the "Ringtone" remix
years.p: Kero Kero Bonito joined too. Brady had already co-produced Charli's "Click".
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Umru teased the remix at a live DJ set on January 24, 2020.

Pitchfork's Jillian Mapes said it recalled PC Music's work and predicted an internet hit; Paper called it a certified hit.

years.h: Atlantic signs the duo, and Brady names his target: Ed Sheeran
years.p: Brady said the ambition was to be as big as Ed Sheeran. They kept their own Dog Show label alongside the deal.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the Atlantic signing in 2020, and Brady's Ed Sheeran line is the quote it prints.

10,000 gecs, three years later, is credited to Dog Show and Atlantic together.

years.src: Wikipedia: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues
years.h: 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues is their first chart entry
years.p: It debuted at No. 198 on the Billboard 200. Injury Reserve, Charli XCX, Black Dresses and Fall Out Boy are on it.
years.xp: Metacritic has it at 81 from seven reviews. NME's Ben Jolley called it an exhilarating snapshot of pop's alternative future.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hand Crushed by a Mallet (remix)
years.h: Patrick Stump sings the intro on "Hand Crushed by a Mallet"
years.p: Pete Wentz proposed it, and the duo got a zip file of Stump singing the intro. Craig Owens and Nicole Dollanganger took the verses and chorus.
years.xp: An animated video followed on August 20, 2020, directed by Dario Alva, and the song hit No. 23 on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs.

years.h: Les puts out "Haunted" solo, and Euphoria picks it up
years.p: It appeared in season 2 of HBO's Euphoria and went RIAA Gold, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Pitchfork gives them the cover, two years after the debut
years.p: The September 7 story is titled "This Is Your Brain on 100 gecs".

years.h: "mememe" arrives with a robed wizard
years.p: The video was the first hint that the second album would be louder.

years.cap: Les and Brady at the 9:30 Club, Washington, October 29, 2021
years.h: The first North American tour ends at Terminal 5, live on Twitch
years.p: The autumn 2021 run was billed as the 10000 gecs tour, with Tony Velour, Underscores, Aaron Cartier and Alice Gas opening.

eras.title: Ten songs in the bin
eras.text: The second album took 18 months and a full restart. The finished record has a nu-metal opener, a real drummer, and none of the nightcore pitch-shifting on Les's voice.

years.cap: 100 gecs at Rock am Ring, Germany, June 2022
years.h: Coachella comes a week after "Doritos & Fritos"
years.p: The single was an alt-rock detour from their signature sound. The music video, released May 16, starred a Danny DeVito impersonator.
years.xp: The year also brought slots at BUKU, Ceremonia, Forecastle, Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza and Governors Ball, plus dates supporting Nine Inch Nails and My Chemical Romance in the US, per Wikipedia. Reading and Leeds came in August.

years.cap: 100 gecs at Capital City Block Party, Seattle, July 24, 2022
years.h: They throw out the first ten songs for the second album
years.p: The FADER has Les saying they thought they had the album, then decided to do something else. Later demo counts run as high as 6,000, per Kerrang.
years.xp:
Les told The FADER that the major-label setting added pressure and that perfectionism was messing with her head.

Brady told Kerrang the process had Darwin vibes, and only the strongest song survives.

years.big: "If it sounds faithful, it's because it sounds good."
q: If it sounds faithful, it's because it sounds good.
years.src: The FADER: 100 gecs discuss channeling · The FADER: 100 gecs, seriously · Kerrang
years.h: Josh Freese plays real drums in the room where System of a Down made Toxicity
years.p: Laura Les on the nu-metal sound, per The FADER. Dylan Brady ran an eight-string guitar through a Boss HM2 into a Dual Rectifier cabinet.
years.xp: Les moved to Los Angeles to work in person with Brady. She also took vocal lessons during the pandemic, and told Kerrang she wanted her pitch-shifting to be more a tool than a crutch.

years.h: Snake Eyes brings Skrillex in on "Torture Me"
years.p: Three songs in 6:04. Pitchfork gave it a 5.6 and called it inconsequential; Rolling Stone said "Hey Big Man" had become a live staple.

years.h: The last single before the album, "Hollywood Baby", makes four best-of lists
years.p: Billboard, i-D, Pitchfork and Slant all put it on their 2023 best-songs lists.

years.src: Wikipedia: 10,000 gecs · Album of the Year: 10,000 gecs · BrooklynVegan: Pitchfork's Top 50
years.h: Pitchfork scores 10,000 gecs 8.2 and ranks it No. 18 of 2023
years.p: Nu-metal, ska and alt-funk in 26 minutes, on Dog Show and Atlantic. It debuted at No. 59 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's review called the record a reevaluation of the most declasse rock genres of the 2000s, per Wikipedia. Metacritic lists 81 from 15 critics. Year-end lists: Stereogum No. 10, NME No. 14, Exclaim! No. 12, Rolling Stone No. 74 of 100.

Reviews weren't uniform: Album of the Year lists the Evening Standard at 20 out of 100.

The cover shows a bridge in Orange, California, which drew less of a following than the tree.

years.src: Interview: 100 Gecs on Shit Posts · Wikipedia: 100 gecs
years.h: Machine Girl opens two nights at Brooklyn Mirage on the biggest tour yet
years.p: Fans bring Game Boys and DS units to the pit, Les told Interview, though she now watches from the side with a big glass of beer.

eras.title: A Black Parade
eras.text: After the album cycle, the duo went back on the road with a band they had opened for three years earlier.

years.cap: 100 gecs opening for My Chemical Romance, September 18, 2022
years.h: Back on the road with My Chemical Romance
years.p: Wikipedia lists the duo on the bill of the 2025 Long Live The Black Parade run, after supporting the band's 2022 reunion shows.
